'''Steven Michael Everitt''' (born August 21, 1970) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Center (gridiron football)|center]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan Wolverines]] from 1989 to 1992. He played professional football as a center and [[offensive guard]] in the NFL for seven seasons, including 46 games for the [[Cleveland Browns]] from 1993 to 1995 and 45 games for the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] from 1997 to 1999.

==Early life==
Everitt was born in [[Miami|Miami, Florida]], in 1970. He attended [[Miami Southridge High School|Southridge High School]] in Miami. He graduated in 1988 and is part of their "Hall of Fame".<ref name=PFR>{{cite web|title=Steve Everitt|publisher=Sports Reference LLC|work=Pro-Football-Reference.com|access-date=April 7, 2015|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/E/EverSt20.htm}}</ref>

==University of Michigan==
Everitt enrolled at the [[University of Michigan]] in 1988 and played [[college football]] as a [[Center (gridiron football)|center]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines football]] teams from 1989 to 1992.<ref name=Roster>{{cite web|title=Michigan Football Roster Database|publisher=University of Michigan, Bentley Historical Library|access-date=April 7, 2015|url=https://bentley.umich.edu/athdept/rosters/football.php}}</ref> As a freshman, Everitt started all 12 games at center for the [[1989 Michigan Wolverines football team]] that compiled a 10–2 record in [[Bo Schembechler]]'s last season as Michigan's head coach.<ref name=t89>{{cite web|url=https://bentley.umich.edu/athdept/football/fbteam/1989fbt.htm|title=1989 Football Team|publisher=University of Michigan, Bentley Historical Library |access-date=April 7, 2015}}</ref> He then shared the starting center role with [[Matt Elliott (American football)|Matt Elliott]] during the 1990 and 1991 seasons.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bentley.umich.edu/athdept/football/fbteam/1990fbt.htm|title=1990 Football Team|publisher=University of Michigan, Bentley Historical Library |access-date=April 7, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://bentley.umich.edu/athdept/football/fbteam/1991fbt.htm|title=1991 Football Team|publisher=University of Michigan, Bentley Historical Library |access-date=April 7, 2015}}</ref> As a senior, he started all 12 games for the undefeated [[1992 Michigan Wolverines football team|1992 Michigan team]] that compiled a 9-0-3 record, outscored opponents 389–198, and defeated [[1992 Washington Huskies football team|Washington]] in the [[1993 Rose Bowl]].<ref name=t92/> He was selected as a first-team player on the [[1992 All-Big Ten Conference football team]].<ref name=t92>{{cite web|url=https://bentley.umich.edu/athdept/football/fbteam/1992fbt.htm|title=1992 Football Team|publisher=University of Michigan, Bentley Historical Library |access-date=April 7, 2015}}</ref>

==Professional football==
Everitt was selected by the [[Cleveland Browns]] in the first round with 14th overall pick of the [[1993 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1993 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1993/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-31 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He played three seasons for the Browns from 1993 to 1995, appearing in 46 games, including 45 games at the team's starting center.<ref name=PFR/> After the Browns moved to Baltimore in [[1996 Baltimore Ravens season|1996]] Everitt was fined $5,000 by the league for wearing a Browns bandana with his Ravens uniform, which he did in protest of the team's relocation .<ref>{{cite news|title=Fine paid, Everitt still takes shots at Modell|newspaper=Toledo Blade|date=November 16, 1997|page=B8|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1350&dat=19971116&id=f3IxAAAAIBAJ&sjid=7A0EAAAAIBAJ&pg=4192,159690&hl=en}}</ref> He appeared in eight games for the Ravens in 1996.<ref name=PFR/>

In March 1997, Everitt signed a five-year $11.5 million contract with the [[Philadelphia Eagles]].<ref>{{cite news|title=He's a center of attention in more ways than one|newspaper=Reading Eagle|author=Steve Patton|date=March 6, 1997|page=C2|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1955&dat=19970306&id=ExtVAAAAIBAJ&sjid=bD0NAAAAIBAJ&pg=2567,4168779&hl=en}}</ref> He spent three years with the Eagles, appearing in 45 games as the team's starting center.<ref name=PFR/> In April 2000, Everitt was released by the Eagles.<ref>{{cite news|title=Eagles release center Everitt, two others as minicamp nears|newspaper=Reading Eagle|date=April 26, 2000|page=D6|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1955&dat=20000426&id=46E0AAAAIBAJ&sjid=TKMFAAAAIBAJ&pg=5989,7366907&hl=en}}</ref>

In June 2000, Everitt signed a two-year contract with the [[St. Louis Rams]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Rams sign McCleon, Everitt|newspaper=The Southeast Missourian|date=June 14, 2000|page=2B|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1893&dat=20000614&id=FYwvAAAAIBAJ&sjid=YNwFAAAAIBAJ&pg=2908,7429415&hl=en}}</ref> He appeared in only four games for the Rams, one as a starter, and all during the [[2000 NFL season]].<ref name=PFR/>

In eight years in the NFL, Everitt appeared in 103 games, 98 of them as a starter, and registered five fumble recoveries.<ref name=PFR/>
